content: Filamin-binding LIM protein 1 (FBLIM1) is a protein encoded by the FBLIM1 gene in humans. This protein contains three distinct structural domains: an N-terminal domain that binds to filamin, a central domain rich in proline residues, and multiple C-terminal LIM domains. FBLIM1 is localized at cell junctions, where it may serve as a molecular link between cell adhesion structures and the actin cytoskeleton. It is thought to play a role in the assembly and stabilization of actin filaments, and it likely contributes to the regulation of cell adhesion, cell morphology, and cell motility. Additionally, this protein is also found in the nucleus, where it may influence the differentiation of cardiomyocytes by interacting with the transcription factor CSX/NKX2-5. Alternative splicing of the FBLIM1 gene generates multiple transcript variants, which encode different isoforms of the protein. FBLIM1 has been demonstrated to interact with several other proteins, including filamin, PLEKHC1, and FLNB.
